review_reference: Coordinator in chat, 2026-11-04, for the owner's launch ("full speed for launch"): "0120 first (prove it, then fix), then the two Outreach blockers"; the number 0120 assigned by the coordinator (0106-0119 belong to other builders). Unsigned until the owner signs.
evidence: In plain words, applying 0120 to production does this. Today every registration of a person into an Outreach campaign is refused, and the field officer sees a server error: the database check that a registration into a campaign is made by a member of that campaign tried to lock the member's row, and production's database settings (the migration login does not bypass row-level security, and campaign memberships have no update rule) made that lock find nothing, so even a real member was refused. Registrations without a campaign were never affected. 0120 changes that one check so it locks the campaign only and reads the membership without locking it. Every rule stays: only a member of the campaign may register into it, only at the campaign's own facility, only while the campaign is active and offers registration, and a registration's campaign cannot be changed afterwards; the refusals keep their codes and messages. A campaign being closed still waits for a registration in progress (and the other way round). Nothing is granted to anyone; no table, row-level security policy, role or permission changes; the Outreach service still cannot change or lock a campaign membership. Shipped in the same backend release: outreach-api answers a refusal that still comes from this check as its own check does (403 OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN_ACCESS_DENIED, 409 OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN_NOT_ACCEPTING_REGISTRATIONS) instead of 500. Today's outreach-api image works on 0120 unchanged. No down migration; rolling the images back leaves 0120 in place and the earlier image works with it. Technical record: 0120_outreach_campaign_registration_lock.sql, written on f11c9ec9 (production 0102-0105) and merged onto staging 6aae042e (0106 OCR worker account, 0107 OCR page allowance, 0108 records processing cover lifetime), is backward compatible. It applies after 0108 unchanged and uses nothing 0106-0119 add: none of 0106, 0107 or 0108 changes an object 0120 reads, pins or replaces (0108 replaces only identity.records_processing_direct_care_cover; 0120's four pinned bodies and the 0105 marker policy measured again on a database built by staging 6aae042e's runner through 0108 with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner are the same md5s as on 0105); runtime-grants.sql's 0120 block follows 0107's (0108 adds no block). It replaces only the body of outreach.validate_registration_campaign_write() (0045; md5 afabd66c378c6e076062f35e80de9cb2 to 2af7fea46fab6a1e03e88999170c51d4): FOR SHARE OF campaign instead of FOR SHARE OF campaign, member; language plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, platform, auth, identity, outreach, owner, ACL (owner only) and the trigger outreach_registration_campaign_validate unchanged; a comment on the function. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0120 block (revoke from PUBLIC on that function, as 0045 did; no grant changes). Preconditions (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501 with nothing applied): 0105's documents_scanner_function_lock policy as the marker; not applied yet; the replaced body and platform.current_membership_id 641989704fea95f885fbc38c6feb5aa5, outreach.context_allows(uuid,text) 1e0e660ba5fd9288f1c1aeca5a7137ac, platform.reject_mutation 398738f39f6eebed2c54da5009495def; the function's attributes; both triggers; the eleven columns read; the read and update policies relied on and no UPDATE or ALL policy on outreach.campaign_members; row-level security enabled and forced on the three tables; the applier is the owner or inherits it with SET. Post-checks: the new md5, attributes, owner, ACL, the trigger, still no UPDATE policy. Locks: SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the function, catalog read locks and the session's own temporary objects; no application table. Proof: to be recorded here by the release commit after the owner signs.
